question: Guru Shashadhar Acharya was awarded the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Folk dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Shashadhar Acharya is a renowned exponent of Seraikella Chhau, a masked dance form from the Seraikella region of Jharkhand, and was conferred the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to Folk dance. (लोक नृत्य — गुरु शशधर आचार्य)

 

• Chhau dance is a semi-classical Indian tribal martial dance with three distinct styles — Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha) — and is recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (inscribed 2010).

 

• Guru Shashadhar Acharya, a fifth-generation Chhau dancer, has trained numerous disciples and worked to popularise Seraikella Chhau nationally and internationally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, conferred for distinguished contribution in fields such as art, literature, science, sports and public affairs.

 

• Other Jharkhand awardees of Padma Shri 2020 included Madhu Mansuri Hasmukh, a Nagpuri folk singer.

 

NOTE

 

• Playing of musical instruments (Option 1): This refers to instrumentalists such as sitar, sarod or santoor players, not to Guru Shashadhar Acharya's field of work.

 

• Classical dance (Option 2): Chhau is generally classified as a folk/tribal dance, not one of the eight recognised classical dance forms of India (such as Bharatanatyam or Kathak).

 

• Hindustani classical singing (Option 4): This is a vocal music tradition, unrelated to Guru Shashadhar Acharya's dance career.

question: Which of the following musicians is associated with the musical instrument Santoor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma was a legendary Indian classical musician credited with popularising the santoor as a solo classical concert instrument. (संतूर — पंडित शिव कुमार शर्मा)

 

• The santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer with numerous strings, traditionally associated with Kashmiri Sufiana music; Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma transformed it into a mainstream Hindustani classical instrument from the 1950s onward.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2001) and was well known for his musical collaborations with flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia under the joint name 'Shiv-Hari'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma and Hariprasad Chaurasia also composed film music together for movies such as *Silsila*, *Lamhe* and *Chandni*.

 

NOTE

 

• Allauddin Khan (Option 1): A legendary sarod and multi-instrument maestro, founder of the Maihar gharana, and guru of Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan.

 

• Annapurna Devi (Option 2): A surbahar (bass sitar) player, daughter of Allauddin Khan, and first wife of Ravi Shankar.

 

• Vilayat Khan (Option 4): A celebrated sitar maestro of the Imdadkhani gharana.

question: What is the atomicity of Chlorine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diatomic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorine exists in its elemental form as Cl₂, a molecule made up of two chlorine atoms bonded together, making it a diatomic element. (क्लोरीन — द्विपरमाणुक)

 

• Atomicity is the total number of atoms present in one molecule of an element. Elements like hydrogen (H₂), oxygen (O₂), nitrogen (N₂) and chlorine (Cl₂) are diatomic.

 

• Chlorine is a halogen (Group 17) and exists as a greenish-yellow, pungent-smelling gas at room temperature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Monoatomic elements include the noble gases — helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, radon.

 

• A triatomic example is ozone (O₃); a tetra-atomic example is phosphorus (P₄); a poly-atomic example is sulphur (S₈).

 

NOTE

 

• Tetra-atomic (Option 1): Applies to molecules with four atoms, such as phosphorus (P₄), not chlorine.

 

• Poly-atomic (Option 3): Applies to molecules with more than four atoms, such as sulphur (S₈).

 

• Monoatomic (Option 4): Applies to single-atom elements such as the noble gases, not chlorine.

question: How many elected members are there in the Legislative Assembly of Telangana till December 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 119.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Telangana Legislative Assembly, formed after the state's bifurcation from Andhra Pradesh in 2014, had 119 elected members till December 2022. (तेलंगाना विधानसभा — 119 निर्वाचित सदस्य)

 

• Telangana has a bicameral legislature at the state level — the directly elected Legislative Assembly along with a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).

 

• Prior to the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 (effective January 2020), the Assembly additionally had one nominated Anglo-Indian member, taking the total strength to 120; this nominated seat was subsequently abolished.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Telangana was formed as India's 29th state on 2 June 2014, carved out of Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Hyderabad serves as the common capital of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (124, 120, 121): These do not match the actual elected strength of 119 members of the Telangana Legislative Assembly as of December 2022.

question: In the year 2022, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare announced a National Suicide Prevention Strategy to bring about a ____________ percent reduction in the suicide mortality rate by 2030.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first National Suicide Prevention Strategy was released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in November 2022, targeting a 10% reduction in the suicide mortality rate by 2030. (आत्महत्या रोकथाम रणनीति — 10 प्रतिशत कमी)

 

• The strategy aligns with global targets under the WHO Mental Health Action Plan and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3.4), both of which push for reduction in premature mortality from non-communicable causes, including suicide.

 

• It lays down time-bound action plans across sectors such as health, education and labour, including establishing effective surveillance mechanisms and psychiatric outpatient services in all districts by 2030.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The strategy's three broad objectives include establishing effective surveillance mechanisms for suicide within the following three years of release.

 

• India observes World Suicide Prevention Day on 10 September every year.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (25%, 20%, 15%): These do not match the officially announced target of a 10% reduction by 2030.

question: The Raut Nacha (Raut Nach) dance is famous in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raut Nacha is a traditional folk dance performed by the Yadav (cowherd) community of Chhattisgarh, usually during the Dev Uthani Ekadashi festival. (राउत नाच — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Dancers perform holding a stick (danda) and wearing peacock-feather headgear, moving to the rhythm of drums like the dhol and nagara, often reciting couplets called Sohar/Diha.

 

• It celebrates the cattle-rearing community's devotion to Lord Krishna and marks the end of the monsoon-season restrictions on cattle-grazing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh include Panthi, Karma, Saila and Suwa.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for folk dances such as Bhangra and Giddha.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas.

 

• Assam (Option 3): Known for the Bihu dance.

question: Being the Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Armed Forces, who takes the salute of the various regiments of the armed forces during the march-past on the occasion of Republic Day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is President of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The President of India, as the Supreme Commander (Commander-in-Chief) of the Armed Forces under Article 53 of the Constitution, takes the salute of the marching regiments during the Republic Day parade. (राष्ट्रपति — सर्वोच्च सेनापति)

 

• The Republic Day parade is held at Kartavya Path, New Delhi, on 26 January every year, commemorating the coming into force of the Constitution of India in 1950.

 

• The President also hosts a chief guest, typically a foreign head of state or government, at the parade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Beating Retreat ceremony, held on 29 January, formally marks the conclusion of the Republic Day celebrations.

 

NOTE

 

• Defence Minister (Option 1), Prime Minister (Option 2), Home Minister (Option 3): None of these constitutional offices holds the position of Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces; only the President does, under Article 53.

question: The famous poet and playwright Rajshekhar was a court poet in the court of which of the following Pratihara kings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendrapala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajshekhar (Rajashekhara), a celebrated Sanskrit poet and dramatist, described himself as the teacher/court poet of the Gurjara-Pratihara king Mahendrapala I. (राजशेखर — महेंद्रपाल, प्रतिहार वंश)

 

• Rajshekhar's notable works include the plays Karpuramanjari, Balabharata (Bala-Ramayana) and Viddhashalabhanjika, and the treatise on poetics Kavyamimamsa.

 

• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty ruled over much of north India between the 8th and 11th centuries CE, with Kannauj as its capital; Mihira Bhoja and his son Mahendrapala I were among its most powerful rulers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pratiharas were one of the three major powers of the 'Tripartite Struggle' for control of Kannauj, along with the Palas of Bengal and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan.

 

NOTE

 

• Rambhadra, Rajapala and Devapala (Options 1, 2 and 3): These names are not the Pratihara ruler with whom Rajshekhar is historically associated; Rajshekhar is specifically linked to Mahendrapala I's court.

question: In which year did the English scientist Michael Faraday discover benzene in illuminating gas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1825.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The English scientist Michael Faraday discovered the compound benzene in 1825, isolating it from the oily residue of illuminating (whale-oil) gas used for street and household lighting in London. (बेंजीन — माइकल फैराडे, 1825)

 

• Faraday initially termed it the 'bicarburet of hydrogen'; its ring structure (C₆H₆) was proposed later, in 1865, by August Kekulé.

 

• Faraday is also renowned for his pioneering work on electromagnetic induction, electrolysis and diamagnetism, and is often called the 'Father of Electricity'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Faraday's laws of electrolysis (1834) laid the quantitative foundation of electrochemistry.

 

• The SI unit of capacitance, the farad, is named in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (1820, 1827, 1822): None of these correspond to the actual year (1825) in which Faraday isolated benzene.

question: In the Later Vedic period, which of the following varnas was primarily engaged in occupations such as agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaishya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Later Vedic period, the Vaishya varna was primarily engaged in agriculture, cattle-rearing (pashupalan) and trade/commerce, forming the economic backbone of society. (वैश्य — कृषि, पशुपालन एवं व्यापार)

 

• The four-fold varna system — Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra — became more rigid during the Later Vedic period (c. 1000-600 BCE), with occupations increasingly becoming hereditary.

 

• Brahmins performed priestly and teaching duties; Kshatriyas were rulers and warriors; Shudras served the other three varnas, primarily through manual labour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later Vedic texts include the Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads, along with the Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.

 

• This period also saw the rise of iron technology, enabling the expansion of agriculture into the Gangetic plains.

 

NOTE

 

• Kshatriya (Option 1): Primarily responsible for warfare, administration and governance.

 

• Brahmin (Option 2): Primarily responsible for religious rituals, teaching and priestly functions.

 

• Shudra (Option 3): Primarily engaged in service to the other three varnas, including manual and menial labour.

question: Identify the meaning of continentality.
option_1: Very hot during winters and very cold during summers
option_2: Very hot during summers and very cold during winters
option_3: Very hot during summers and lots of rain
option_4: Very cold during winters and not hot during summers
solution_text:
The correct answer is Very hot during summers and very cold during winters.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Continentality refers to the degree to which a region's climate is influenced by its distance from the moderating effect of the sea, resulting in extreme temperature variation — very hot summers and very cold winters. (महाद्वीपीयता — अत्यधिक तापांतर)

 

• Areas with high continentality (interior of large landmasses, far from coasts) experience a large annual range of temperature, because land heats up and cools down faster than water.

 

• Coastal areas, by contrast, show low continentality and more moderate, equable climates due to the sea's moderating influence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Regions like Siberia and Central Asia show extreme continentality, with very hot summers and bitterly cold winters.

 

• Maritime/coastal climates (e.g., the British Isles) show low continentality, with mild summers and winters.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4: These describe inaccurate variations of the actual meaning of continentality, which specifically refers to hot summers combined with cold winters in landlocked, interior locations.

question: Where and when were the first Khelo India University Games held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha, 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Khelo India University Games (KIUG) were held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, from 22 February to 1 March 2020. (खेलो इंडिया विश्वविद्यालय खेल — ओडिशा, 2020)

 

• The event was organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in collaboration with the Association of Indian Universities (AIU), and was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

 

• Panjab University, Chandigarh, topped the medal tally at the inaugural edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khelo India programme was launched in 2018 to revive sports culture in India at the grassroots level.

 

• The Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) is a separate, school-level component of the same overall scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra, 2019; Punjab, 2019; Kerala, 2020 (Options 1, 3 and 4): These states/years do not correspond to the actual venue and year of the first Khelo India University Games.

question: (As of November 2021) how many cities have been identified for ring roads under Phase-I of the 'Bharatmala Pariyojana' to reduce traffic in various cities across India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Phase-I of the Bharatmala Pariyojana, 28 cities across India had been identified for the construction of ring roads/bypasses (as of November 2021) to help decongest urban traffic. (भारतमाला परियोजना — 28 शहर, रिंग रोड)

 

• Bharatmala Pariyojana is an umbrella road and highways development programme launched by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in 2017, focused on optimising the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across India.

 

• The programme aims to develop about 26,000 km of economic corridors, along with feeder routes, inter-corridor routes, national corridor efficiency improvements, border/international connectivity roads, coastal/port connectivity roads and expressways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatmala Pariyojana is implemented mainly by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

 

• It succeeded the earlier National Highways Development Project (NHDP).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (33, 41, 21): These figures do not match the officially identified count of 28 cities for ring roads under Phase-I.

question: Which species of mangrove tree found in the Sundarbans of India and Bangladesh is scientifically known as 'Heritiera fomes'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sundari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mangrove tree species scientifically named Heritiera fomes is commonly called Sundari, and it is this tree that gives the Sundarbans ('forest of Sundari') its name. (सुंदरी वृक्ष — Heritiera fomes)

 

• Sundari trees are found extensively in the Sundarbans mangrove forest, spread across the delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna river system in India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh.

 

• The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, along with other mangrove species like Gewa (Excoecaria agallocha) and Goran (Ceriops decandra).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sundarbans National Park (India) was declared a Tiger Reserve in 1973, a National Park in 1984, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

 

NOTE

 

• Kachnar (Option 1): A flowering tree (Bauhinia variegata), not a mangrove/Sundarbans species.

 

• Kusum (Option 3): A tree (Schleichera oleosa) valued for lac cultivation, not the source of the Sundarbans' name.

 

• Arjun (Option 4): A medicinal tree (Terminalia arjuna) found along riverbanks, unrelated to Heritiera fomes.

question: Who introduced the Zamindari Settlement as a measure of land revenue administration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Cornwallis, Governor-General of Bengal, introduced the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) of land revenue in 1793, making zamindars the owners of land who were required to pay a fixed revenue to the British government. (स्थायी बंदोबस्त — लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस)

 

• Under this system, the revenue demand was fixed permanently, meaning it would never be revised even if agricultural output increased, benefiting the zamindars but leaving cultivators (ryots) with no security of tenure.

 

• The Permanent Settlement was implemented mainly in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, and parts of Uttar Pradesh (Banaras region).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other land revenue systems introduced by the British include the Ryotwari System (Madras and Bombay presidencies, associated with Thomas Munro/Alexander Read) and the Mahalwari System (North-Western Provinces, Punjab).

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 1): Known for the Vernacular Press Act (1878) and the Second Anglo-Afghan War.

 

• Lord Curzon (Option 2): Known for the Partition of Bengal (1905) and the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act.

 

• Lord Wellesley (Option 4): Known for introducing the Subsidiary Alliance System.

question: Who among the following is India's second Grandmaster after Viswanathan Anand?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} @font-face { font-family: 'Harikris'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARIKRIS.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>P. Harikrishna
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dibyendu Barua.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dibyendu Barua became India's second Grandmaster (GM) in 1991, after Viswanathan Anand, who became India's first Grandmaster in 1988. (दिब्येंदु बरुआ — भारत के दूसरे ग्रैंडमास्टर)

 

• Barua, from West Bengal, is also a chess arbiter and administrator, and has served in leadership roles with the All India Chess Federation (AICF).

 

• Viswanathan Anand remains India's most celebrated chess player, a five-time World Chess Champion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since Anand and Barua, India has produced many more Grandmasters, including P. Harikrishna, Krishnan Sasikiran and R. Praggnanandhaa, positioning India among the top chess nations.

 

NOTE

 

• P. Harikrishna (Option 1): A leading Indian Grandmaster, but became a GM later than Barua, not India's second.

 

• Abhijit Kunte (Option 3): An Indian Grandmaster, but not the second to attain the title.

 

• Krishnan Sasikiran (Option 4): A strong Indian Grandmaster, but achieved the GM title after Barua.

question: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) scheme was launched by which ministry of the Government of India?
option_1: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
option_4: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) was launched in 2008 by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India. (प्रधानमंत्री रोजगार सृजन कार्यक्रम — सूक्ष्म, लघु और मध्यम उद्यम मंत्रालय)

 

• PMEGP is a credit-linked subsidy scheme aimed at generating self-employment opportunities through the establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, helping traditional artisans and unemployed youth.

 

• It was formed by merging two earlier schemes — the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) and the Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana (PMRY).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMEGP is implemented at the national level by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), an agency under the Ministry of MSME.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 2): Handles the Union Budget and financial policy, not the direct implementation of PMEGP.

 

• Ministry of Rural Development (Option 3): Implements rural welfare schemes such as MGNREGA and PMAY-G, not PMEGP.

 

• Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Option 4): Deals with urban housing and city development schemes, not PMEGP.

question: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of ______ Articles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 395.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution, as originally adopted on 26 November 1949 and enforced from 26 January 1950, consisted of 395 Articles, organised into 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. (भारतीय संविधान — मूलतः 395 अनुच्छेद)

 

• The Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, with Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

 

• Over time, through numerous amendments, the Constitution has grown; it currently has about 470 Articles in 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country in the world.

 

• It draws provisions from various sources, including the Government of India Act, 1935, and the constitutions of other countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (385, 365, 375): These figures do not match the actual original number of Articles (395) in the Indian Constitution.

question: Which cells, also called neurilemma cells, are the main glial cells in the PNS and play an essential role in the survival and functions of neurons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Schwann cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Schwann cells, also called neurilemma cells, are the principal glial (supporting) cells of the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS), essential for the survival, insulation (myelination) and functioning of neurons. (श्वान कोशिकाएं — परिधीय तंत्रिका तंत्र)

 

• These cells wrap around the axons of peripheral neurons, forming the myelin sheath, which increases the speed of nerve impulse conduction and also assists in nerve regeneration after injury.

 

• They are named after the German physiologist Theodor Schwann, who discovered them in the 19th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In the Central Nervous System (CNS), the equivalent myelinating cells are called Oligodendrocytes, not Schwann cells.

 

• Other glial cells include Astrocytes, Microglia and Ependymal cells (all in the CNS).

 

NOTE

 

• Bipolar cells (Option 1): A type of retinal neuron involved in vision, not a glial cell of the PNS.

 

• Ganglion cells (Option 2): Neurons found in the retina (and elsewhere) that transmit signals; not glial support cells.

 

• Photoreceptor cells (Option 4): Light-sensitive neurons (rods and cones) in the retina, unrelated to PNS glial support.

question: According to dietary guidelines recommended by physicians, the RDA for cholesterol intake in healthy adults and children above four years of age is ______ mg/day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 300.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per dietary guidelines recommended by physicians/nutrition bodies, the Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) for cholesterol intake in healthy adults and children above four years of age is 300 mg/day. (कोलेस्ट्रॉल — 300 mg/दिन)

 

• This guideline aims to limit dietary cholesterol intake in order to reduce the risk of cardiovascular diseases, such as atherosclerosis and coronary heart disease.

 

• Such guidelines are issued in India by bodies such as the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN), under the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), as part of nutrient requirement recommendations for Indians.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cholesterol is broadly of two types when discussing blood lipid profile — LDL ('bad' cholesterol) and HDL ('good' cholesterol).

 

• Diets high in saturated fats and trans fats tend to raise LDL cholesterol levels, increasing cardiovascular risk.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (600, 500, 400): These values exceed the recommended daily limit of 300 mg for cholesterol intake.

question: On 21 November 2022, who assumed charge as the new Election Commissioner (EC) of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arun Goel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arun Goel, a retired IAS officer, assumed charge as Election Commissioner of India on 21 November 2022. (अरुण गोयल — निर्वाचन आयुक्त)

 

• His appointment was notable for being processed and finalised within a single day, shortly before the Supreme Court was scheduled to hear a case on the appointment process for Election Commissioners.

 

• At the time, the Election Commission of India (ECI) comprised the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners, operating as a multi-member body under Article 324 of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Election Commissioners were, at the time, appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers; the Supreme Court, in March 2023, ruled that a committee comprising the PM, Leader of Opposition and CJI should advise on such appointments until Parliament legislates otherwise.

 

NOTE

 

• Manoj Kumar (Option 1): Not associated with this appointment; a distractor option.

 

• Rajiv Kumar (Option 2): Became an Election Commissioner earlier (2020) and later Chief Election Commissioner (2022), not the one who joined on 21 November 2022.

 

• Anup Chandra Pandey (Option 4): Was already serving as an Election Commissioner (since 2021) before Arun Goel's appointment.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the characteristics of the new agricultural strategy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Use of organic manures.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New Agricultural Strategy, introduced in India in the mid-1960s (commonly associated with the Green Revolution), was characterised by the use of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, extensive/assured irrigation and pesticides — not primarily organic manures. (नई कृषि रणनीति — हरित क्रांति)

 

• The strategy was pioneered with the guidance of agricultural scientists like Dr. M. S. Swaminathan, often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India', and was implemented from the Third Five-Year Plan period onward.

 

• It significantly boosted wheat and rice production, particularly in states like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, helping India achieve self-sufficiency in foodgrains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution had certain drawbacks, including soil degradation, over-extraction of groundwater, and regional/crop imbalances, which later spurred interest in organic and sustainable farming.

 

NOTE

 

• Use of chemical fertilisers (Option 1): A core, defining feature of the new agricultural strategy.

 

• Use of hybrid seeds (Option 2): HYV/hybrid seeds were central to the strategy's higher productivity.

 

• Extensive irrigation (Option 3): Assured, extensive irrigation was essential to support HYV seeds and multiple cropping.

question: Who among the following is a Nobel laureate, who is also known as the father of microfinance systems?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Yunus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi economist, is widely known as the 'father of microfinance', for founding the Grameen Bank in 1983, pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance for the poor, especially women, without requiring collateral. (मुहम्मद यूनुस — सूक्ष्म वित्त के जनक)

 

• He and Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 'for their efforts to create economic and social development from below'.

 

• His microfinance model has been replicated in numerous countries as a tool for poverty alleviation and women's economic empowerment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad Yunus later went on to head the interim government of Bangladesh as its Chief Adviser from August 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• Amartya Sen (Option 1): An Indian economist awarded the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (1998) for his work on welfare economics, not microfinance.

 

• Raghuram Rajan (Option 2): An Indian economist and former RBI Governor, not a Nobel laureate.

 

• Sandra Rotman (Option 4): A Canadian philanthropist, not a Nobel laureate associated with microfinance.

question: In ________, Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the Partition of Bengal in 1905, dividing the large Bengal Presidency into two provinces — Eastern Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and the rest of Bengal (Bihar, Orissa, West Bengal; Hindu-majority). (बंगाल विभाजन — 1905, लॉर्ड कर्ज़न)

 

• The partition, ostensibly for administrative convenience, was widely seen as a strategy of 'divide and rule' to weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal.

 

• It sparked the Swadeshi Movement and a boycott of foreign goods, marking a significant escalation in the Indian freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Due to intense public protest, the Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911, announced at the Delhi Durbar during the reign of King George V.

 

• The capital of India was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (1907, 1906, 1911): 1911 was the year the partition was annulled, not announced; 1906 and 1907 do not correspond to the announcement of the partition.

question: Who among the following is appointed as new Attorney General for India in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R Venkataramani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Senior advocate R Venkataramani was appointed as the Attorney General for India in September 2022, taking charge effective 1 October 2022, succeeding K K Venugopal. (अटॉर्नी जनरल — आर वेंकटरमणी)

 

• The Attorney General for India is the highest law officer of the country, appointed by the President of India under Article 76 of the Constitution, and serves as the government's chief legal adviser.

 

• The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament, without voting rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General assist the Attorney General in legal duties, though (unlike the Attorney General) they are not offices envisaged directly under the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• K K Venugopal (Option 2): Served as Attorney General for India before R Venkataramani, from 2017 to September 2022.

 

• Fali Sam Nariman (Option 3): An eminent Indian jurist, but never served as Attorney General for India.

 

• Harish Salve (Option 4): A prominent Indian senior advocate, who previously served as Solicitor General of India (not Attorney General).
